'''Caucher Birkar''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} ({{langx|ku|کۆچەر بیرکار|lit=migrant mathematician|translit=Koçer Bîrkar}}; born '''Fereydoun Derakhshani''' ({{Langx|ku|فەرەیدوون درەخشانی}}، {{langx|fa|فریدون درخشانی}}); July 1978) is a UK-based Iranian Kurdish and British  mathematician<ref>{{Cite web |last=York |first=University of |title=Professor Caucher Birkar |url=https://www.york.ac.uk/maths/about/equality-diversity-inclusion/celebrating-mathematicians/professor-caucher-birkar/ |access-date=2024-11-08 |website=University of York |language=en|quote=Professor Caucher Birkar is an Iranian Kurdish and British mathematician, who won the Fields Medal for his contributions to algebraic geometry in 2018.}}</ref> (born in Iran) and a professor at [[Tsinghua University]]. He is also an Honorary Professor at the [[University of Nottingham]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/news/fields-medal-winner-appointed-honorary-professor
|title=Fields Medal winner appointed Honorary Professor
|website=University of Nottingham|language=en|access-date=22 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cam.ac.uk/research/news/cambridge-mathematician-awarded-2018-fields-medal|title=Cambridge mathematician awarded 2018 Fields Medal|date=1 August 2018|website=University of Cambridge}}</ref>

Birkar is an important contributor to modern [[birational geometry]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/IMU/Prizes/Fields/2018/Birkar-Citation.pdf|title=Birkar Citation|year=2018|website=International Mathematical Union|page=2|others=Birkar long citation.}}</ref> In 2010 he received the [[Leverhulme Prize]] in mathematics and statistics for his contributions to [[algebraic geometry]],<ref name="auto">{{cite web |url=http://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/news/awards/plp.cfm |title=Philip Leverhulme Prizes |access-date=30 December 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130610153414/http://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/news/awards/plp.cfm |archive-date=10 June 2013 }}</ref> and in 2016, shared the AMS Moore Prize for the article "Existence of minimal models for varieties of log general type".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=2873|title=American Mathematical Society|website=www.ams.org|access-date=1 August 2018}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in 2018, "for his proof of boundedness of [[Fano varieties]] and contributions to the [[minimal model program]]".<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last1=Davis|first1=Nicola|last2=Zhou|first2=Naaman|date=1 August 2018|title=Former refugee among winners of Fields medal – the 'Nobel prize for maths'|work=[[The Guardian]]|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2018/aug/01/former-refugee-among-winners-of-fields-medal-the-nobel-prize-for-maths|access-date=3 January 2021}}</ref> In his office at the university, Birkar has two photographs of [[Alexander Grothendieck]], his favorite mathematician, who like Birkar, was a refugee and Fields medalist.<ref name=":1" />

Birkar maintains strong ties to his Kurdish heritage and actively encourages Kurdish identity while also separating it from nationalism and politics. According to Birkar, his strong Kurdish identity is not a part of nationalism nor politics and he is not striving for such achievements.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZIIu63IMq4U |title=کۆچەر بیرکار یەکێک لە 50 کاریگارترین بیرمەندەکانی جیهان|website=www.youtube.com|date=16 September 2022 |access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref> This can be a reflection of his name change to Caucher Birkar which roughly translates into ”the Migrating Mathematician”.

==Early life and education==
Birkar is a [[Kurdish people|Kurd]], born in 1978 in [[Marivan County]], Kurdistan province, [[Iran]], on a subsistence farm, and raised during the [[Iran-Iraq War]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|last=Hartnett|first=Kevin|date=1 August 2018|title=An Innovator Who Brings Order to an Infinitude of Equations|work=[[Quanta Magazine]]|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/caucher-birkar-who-fled-war-and-found-asylum-wins-fields-medal-20180801/|access-date=3 January 2021}}</ref> He had five siblings,<ref name=":1" /> and learned a lot of mathematics from his brothers during the first years of school.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Caucher Birkar wins 2018 Fields Medal {{!}} Features: Faculty Insights|url=https://www.maths.cam.ac.uk/features/professor-caucher-birkar-wins-2018-fields-medal|url-status=live|access-date=2 January 2022|website=[[Cambridge University]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181013113530/http://www.maths.cam.ac.uk/features/professor-caucher-birkar-wins-2018-fields-medal|archive-date=13 October 2018}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Following his graduation from high school,<ref name=":1" /> Birkar studied mathematics at the [[University of Tehran]] where he received his bachelor's degree. He was awarded the third prize in the [[International Mathematics Competition for University Students]] in 2000<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ucl.ac.uk/~ucahjej/imc/imc2000/results.html|title=IMC – International Mathematics Competition for University Students|first=C|last=Draganova|website=www.ucl.ac.uk|access-date=2 August 2018}}</ref> and, shortly after, while still studying in the university, relocated to the UK as a [[refugee]] and asked for [[political asylum]].<ref name=BBCFields>[https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-45032422 Fields medal: UK refugee wins 'biggest maths prize'], by Paul Rincon, at [[BBC.co.uk]]; published 1 August 2018; retrieved 1 August 2018</ref> In 2001–2004 Birkar was a PhD student at the [[University of Nottingham]].<ref name=cbphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Nottingham|url=https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~cb496/finalthesis.pdf|title=Topics in modern algebraic geometry|first=Caucher|last=Birkar|date=2004|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.421475}}|website=cam.ac.uk|access-date=18 April 2019|archive-date=17 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220517000129/https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~cb496/finalthesis.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2003 he was awarded the Cecil King Travel Scholarship by the [[London Mathematical Society]] as the most promising PhD student.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/cecil-king-travel-scholarship|title=Cecil King Travel Scholarship in Mathematics|access-date=3 August 2018}}</ref> Upon emigrating to the UK he changed his name to Caucher Birkar, which means "migrant mathematician" in [[Kurdish languages|Kurdish]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://kayhan.london/fa/1397/05/11/%D9%85%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%81%DB%8C%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%B2-%DA%A9%D9%88%DA%86%D8%B1-%D8%A8%DB%8C%D8%B1%DA%A9%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%B6%DB%8C%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A8%D9%87-%D8%B3|title=مدال "فیلدز" کوچر بیرکار ریاضیدان به سرقت رفت اما افتخارش برای ایرانیان ماندنی است|last=لندن|first=کیهان|date=2 August 2018|access-date=7 August 2018|language=fa-IR}}</ref>

==Research and career==
<!-- Birkar's main area of interest is [[algebraic geometry]], in particular, higher dimensional [[birational geometry]]. He studied fundamental aspects of key problems in modern mathematics such as [[Minimal model program|minimal models]], [[Fano varieties]], [[Singular point of an algebraic variety|singularities]], and [[Linear system of divisors|linear systems]]. His theories provided solutions of various long-standing conjectures.{{fact|date=August 2018}} -->

Together with Paolo Cascini, [[Christopher Hacon]] and [[James McKernan]], Birkar settled several conjectures including existence of log [[Flip (algebraic geometry)|flips]], finite generation of log [[canonical ring]]s, and existence of minimal models for varieties of log general type, building upon earlier work of [[Vyacheslav Shokurov]] and of Hacon and McKernan.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Birkar | first1 = Caucher
 | last2 = Cascini | first2 = Paolo
 | last3 = Hacon | first3 = Christopher D.
 | last4 = McKernan | first4 = James
 | doi = 10.1090/S0894-0347-09-00649-3
 | issue = 2
 | journal = [[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]
 | mr = 2601039
 | pages = 405–468
 | title = Existence of minimal models for varieties of log general type
 | url = https://scholar.archive.org/work/v3jddl754bhdzm3z62zba6ahiu
 | volume = 23
 | year = 2010| arxiv = math/0610203
 | bibcode = 2010JAMS...23..405B
 }}</ref> <!-- He also showed that the minimal model conjecture follows from the [[abundance conjecture]] and established links between the former conjecture and various other notions such as log canonical thresholds and [[Oscar Zariski|Zariski]] decompositions.{{fact|date=August 2018}} -->

In the setting of [[log canonical singularity|log canonical singularities]], he proved existence of log flips along with key cases of the minimal model and [[abundance conjecture]]s.  (This was also proved independently by Hacon and [[Chenyang Xu]].)<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1007/s10240-012-0039-5|title = Existence of log canonical flips and a special LMMP| journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS| volume=115| pages=325–368|year = 2012|last1 = Birkar|first1 = Caucher| arxiv=1104.4981|s2cid = 121722661}}</ref>

In a different direction, he studied the old problem of [[Iitaka]] on effectivity of Iitaka fibrations induced by pluri-canonical systems on varieties of non-negative [[Kodaira dimension]]. The problem consists of two halves: one related to general fibres of the fibration and one related to the base of the fibration. Birkar and Zhang co-solved the second half of the problem, hence essentially reducing Iitaka's problem to the special case of Kodaira dimension zero.<ref>C. Birkar, D.-Q. Zhang, Effectivity of Iitaka fibrations and pluricanonical systems of polarized pairs. To appear in Pub. Math IHES.</ref>

In more recent work, Birkar studied Fano varieties and singularities of linear systems. He has solved several fundamental problems such as Shokurov's conjecture on boundedness of complements, and the Borisov–Alexeev–Borisov conjecture on boundedness of Fano varieties.<ref>C. Birkar, [https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.05765  Anti-pluricanonical systems on Fano varieties.] arXiv:1603.05765</ref><ref>C. Birkar, [https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.05543  Singularities of linear systems and boundedness of Fano varieties.] arXiv:1609.05543.</ref> <!-- This direction is viewed to have fundamental applications in birational geometry. Birkar answered a question of [[Gang Tian]] on alpha-invariants and answered a question of [[Jean-Pierre Serre]] on Jordan property of [[Cremona group]]s building on the work of [[Yuri Gennadyevich Prokhorov|Yuri Prokhorov]] and [[Constantin Shramov]].{{fact|date=August 2018}} -->In 2018, Birkar was given the [[Fields Medal]] for his work on [[Fano varieties]] and other contributions to the minimal model problem.<ref name=":0" /> In a video made available by the [[Simons Foundation]], Birkar expressed hope that his Fields Medal will put "just a little smile on the lips" of the world's estimated 40 million Kurds.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Castelvecchi|first=Davide|date=1 August 2018|title=Number-theory prodigy among winners of most coveted prize in mathematics|journal=Nature|volume=560|issue=7717|pages=152–153|pmid=30087472|doi=10.1038/d41586-018-05864-w|bibcode=2018Natur.560..152C|doi-access=|s2cid=51935597 }}</ref> Birkar's Fields Medal was stolen on the same day it was awarded to him.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/aug/01/fields-medal-award-stolen-brazil-maths-prize|title=World's most prestigious maths medal is stolen alongside his wallet minutes after professor wins it|last=Phillips|first=Dom|date=1 August 2018|website=The Guardian}}</ref> In a special ceremony at ICM 2018, Birkar was presented with a replacement medal, leading to quips he was the first person to receive the Fields Medal ''twice''.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.icm2018.org/wp/2018/08/04/im-more-famous-now-than-i-would-be-jokes-birkar/|title="I'm more famous now than I would be", jokes Birkar|website=ICM 2018|date=4 August 2018|access-date=10 November 2018|archive-date=8 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200808210505/http://www.icm2018.org/wp/2018/08/04/im-more-famous-now-than-i-would-be-jokes-birkar/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Birkar is also active in the field of birational geometry over fields of positive characteristic. His work together with work of Hacon-Xu nearly completes the minimal model program for 3-folds over fields of characteristic at least 7.<ref>C. Birkar, [http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/AnnalesENS/4_49/html/ens_ann-sc_49_169-212.php Existence of flips and minimal models for 3-folds in char p.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180809030155/http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/AnnalesENS/4_49/html/ens_ann-sc_49_169-212.php |date=9 August 2018 }} Annales scientifiques de l'ENS 49 (2016), 169–212.</ref>

In 2021, Birkar joined [[Tsinghua University]] as a tenured professor. In 2025, he was elected as a foreign academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.caixinglobal.com/2021-06-26/fields-medal-winner-caucher-birkar-joins-chinas-tsinghua-university-101732182.html|title=Fields Medal Winner Caucher Birkar Joins China’s Tsinghua University|first=Wei|last=Han|newspaper=Caixin Global|date=2021-06-26|access-date=2025-12-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cas.cn/tz/202511/t20251121_5089455.shtml|title=关于公布2025年中国科学院院士增选当选院士名单的公告|trans-title=Announcement on the List of Newly Elected Academicians of the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 2025|lang=zh|date=2025-11-21|newspaper=cas.cn|access-date=2025-12-22}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
* 2010 [[Leverhulme Prize]] in mathematics and statistics for "his outstanding contributions to fundamental research in algebraic geometry"<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://burttotaro.wordpress.com/2010/11/22/caucher-birkar-awarded-2010-philip-leverhulme-prize/|title=Caucher Birkar has been awarded 2010 Philip Leverhulme prize|date=22 November 2010|website=wordpress.com|access-date=1 August 2018}}</ref>
* 2010 Prize of the Fondation Sciences Mathématiques de Paris<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sciencesmaths-paris.fr/en/Researchers%20and%20Students-285.htm |title=The Foundation's Prize Laureates |access-date=1 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140317002744/http://www.sciencesmaths-paris.fr/en/Researchers%20and%20Students-285.htm |archive-date=17 March 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2016 AMS [[Moore Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=2873|title=American Mathematical Society|website=www.ams.org|access-date=2 August 2018}}</ref>
* 2018 [[Fields Medal]]<ref name=":0" />
* 2019 Honorary Doctorate of the [[Salahaddin University-Erbil|Salahaddin University]], Erbil<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/culture/fa9a3845-85ae-4986-b6af-7f2127580e74|title=University in Kurdistan awards honorary doctorate to Fields Medal laureate|website=Kurdistan24|language=en|access-date=31 July 2019}}</ref>
